newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait-Iran to build $70 million steel mill.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait-Iran to build $70 million steel mill.

text.p: The National Iranian Steel Company (Nisco) and private Kuwaiti investors are close to setting up a $70 million steel reinforced bar mill in Kuwait, Iran's envoy to Kuwait said on Wednesdsay.

"There has been approval for this and many related issues have been finalised," GholamAli Sanati told Reuters. "What remains now is financial arrangements and in the near future we will start with setting up this project."
The proposed mill is expected to produce about 300,000 tonnes a year while Kuwait's annual consumption is estimated at 400,000 tonnes. The production will be consumed domestically.
Nisco has a 49 percent stake in the project while Kuwaiti investors hold 51 percent.
Sanati said that preliminary talks have also been held with Kuwait for jointly building two cement plants in Kuwait.

The trade balance between Kuwait and non-Arab Iran is in favour of the Gulf Arab state which exports to the Islamic republic refined oil products worth some $200 million a year while Iranian exports to Kuwait are worth about $85 million.
Tehran last month signed a contract with the state Kuwait Petroleum Corp for the purchase of 750,000 tonnes of gas oil and kerosene during 1997, Kuwaiti and Iranian officials said.

Cooperation in the energy field between the two members of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) will be discussed in detail later this week when Iran's oil minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh starts a visit to Kuwait on Saturday.
